Brown]] {{nowrap|(Kannapolis, North Carolina)}} | college = [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]] | draftyear = 1985 | draftround = 1 | draftpick = 15 | pastteams = * [[Kansas City Chiefs]] ({{NFL Year|1985}}) * [[Los Angeles Raiders]] ({{NFL Year|1987}}, {{NFL Year|1989|1993}}) * [[Washington Football Team|Washington Redskins]] ({{NFL Year|1994}}) | highlights = * [[Pro Bowl]] ([[1992 Pro Bowl|1991]]) * Second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] ([[1984 College Football All-America Team|1984]]) * 2× First-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] ([[1983 All-Atlantic Coast Conference football team|1983]], [[1984 All-Atlantic Coast Conference football team|1984]]) * [[North Carolina Tar Heels football#Honored jerseys|North Carolina Tar Heels Jersey No. 12]] honored | statlabel1 = [[Reception (American football)|Receptions]] | statvalue1 = 212 | statlabel2 = Receiving yards | statvalue2 = 2,360 | statlabel3 = Rushing yards | statvalue3 = 241 | statlabel4 = Total [[touchdown]]s | statvalue4 = 20 | pfr = HortEt00 }} '''Ethan Shane Horton''' (born December 19, 1962) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played one season as a [[running back]] for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] (1985), and seven seasons as a tight end for the [[Los Angeles Raiders]] (1987, 1989–1993), and the [[Washington Redskins]] (1994). ==College career== Horton played [[college football]] at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]], where he was an all-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] running back and 1984 ACC Player of the Year. In 1981, he was named the co-[[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the [[1981 Gator Bowl|Gator Bowl]], and in 1982 he shared MVP honors with two teammates in the [[1982 Sun Bowl|Sun Bowl]]. Horton rushed for 1,107 yards as a junior and 1,247 as a senior. Overall, he rushed for 3,074 yards, caught 46 passes for 495 yards, and scored 27 touchdowns.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/ethan-horton-1.html|title = Ethan Horton College Stats}} ==Professional career== Horton was selected by the Chiefs in the first round with the 15th overall pick of the [[1985 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |title=1985 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1985/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He caught 28 passes in his rookie season, but had a dismal year running the ball, finishing the season with just 146 rushing yards.{{Cite web |title=Ex-Chief Horton Now Wearing Out Kansas City |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1991/12/29/ex-chief-horton-now-wearing-out-kansas-city/ |website=Chicago Tribune|date=December 29, 1991 }} He was widely considered a bust and cut by the Chiefs at the end of the year. Horton managed to sign on with the Raiders in 1987, but played in just four games and was cut during training camp in 1988. He then returned to North Carolina as an athletic counselor, but was called back to the Raiders in 1989 by owner [[Al Davis]], who had him converted to the tight end position. Although he saw limited playing time in 1989, this ultimately paid off as he caught 33 passes in 1990, and scored a 41-yard touchdown reception in the team's divisional playoff win in the postseason. Horton had his best season in 1991, when he caught 53 passes for 650 yards and five touchdowns, which earned him his only career selection to the pro bowl. He added 77 more receptions with his next two years on the Raiders, and finished his NFL career with the Redskins in 1994.
